claims.text: Rainier Avenue South & South Othello Street had 12 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Rainier Avenue South & South Othello Street's own: the city's record places 113 of the 135 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $822,000 a year.
32% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehcile struck pedestrian” crashes, against 7% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $123,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Lighting would avoid about 0.3 crashes a year (CMF 7774, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $96,000 a year; check on site: the corner has no street lighting now.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for Rainier Avenue South, South Garden Street, South Othello Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
